en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape, which you can clearly observe from Legazpi City.
Visitors can observe massive stalactites and stalagmites hanging from the ceiling inside the Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park.
You can see Volcano Island, which contains Main Crater, sitting right in the middle of Taal Lake in Batangas.
Hikers in Bukidnon can spot the massive, foul-smelling Rafflesia schadenbergiana flower blooming on the forest floor.
During the dry season, the grass covering the Chocolate Hills in Bohol turns brown, resembling giant chocolate mounds.
Scuba divers in Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park can observe vibrant coral reefs and sea turtles swimming underwater.
From November to February, the amihan monsoon brings cool, dry northeast winds that you can feel across the Philippines.
Trekkers climbing Mount Pulag can walk through a mossy forest where thick moss covers the trees and rocks.
Birdwatchers in the Mount Apo Natural Park can observe the rare Philippine Eagle with its distinctive shaggy crest.
You can see the powerful, twin cascades of Maria Cristina Falls dropping into the Agus River in Lanao del Norte.
Tourists in the Hundred Islands National Park can observe tall limestone karst formations rising directly from the Lingayen Gulf.
Observers in Ifugao can see the Banaue Rice Terraces carved into steep mountain slopes, following the natural land contours.
